title: Dental veneers in Mohandessin
description: Explore porcelain veneers in Mohandessin, including tooth preparation, shade selection, alternatives and the long-term care to discuss before treatment.
answer: Veneers are thin porcelain shells bonded to the front of selected teeth to change their shade or shape. At {{brand}} in Mohandessin, adults with healthy teeth and gums can discuss veneers, including their role in a Hollywood smile design. Enamel, bite and future maintenance all affect suitability.
preparation: We check your teeth, gums and bite, and discuss the changes you would like to make.
howPerformed: Veneers are thin porcelain shells bonded to the front of teeth to change their colour, shape or appearance. We assess your teeth and gums first and explain whether veneers suit your concerns.
followup: Temporary sensitivity can follow preparation and fitting. We will explain cleaning, eating and what to do if your bite feels uncomfortable. Regular dental reviews remain important.
suitability: Veneers may suit adults with healthy teeth and gums who want to address colour, chips, gaps or shape. Grinding, bite problems and the amount of healthy enamel affect suitability. We also discuss alternatives.
outlook: The change is visible once the veneers are fitted. How long they last depends on your bite, habits and care. We will explain how to protect them and when to return for dental reviews.

faqs.a: The shade, shape and proportions all affect the look. We discuss your preferences and review the proposed design with you before fitting, aiming for a result that fits your smile.

Veneers often require removing some enamel, which cannot grow back. The amount depends on your teeth and the design. We explain this before you decide, along with alternatives and the possibility of future repair or replacement.

Porcelain veneers may last ten to fifteen years, although lifespan varies. Oral hygiene, regular dental reviews and managing tooth grinding all matter. Individual veneers may need repair or replacement sooner.
Tell the team about dental sensitivity. The examination helps decide whether local anaesthesia or other comfort measures are appropriate.
